rules.rationale: Oxide anions carried the largest positive lift in development; oxygen's high polarizability raises phonon DOS peaks.
Moderate concentration balances polarizability and bonding complexity, matching the strongest observed candidates.
Mid mean Z covers oxides and moderately concentrated compositions.
Lanthanides were absent from the top candidates; f-electron contributions complicate phonon spectra.

skills.hypothesis: Transfers oxide polarizability and moderate concentration from the strongest development candidates; fails if lanthanide-free oxides saturate early.

rules.rationale: Light nonmetals lowered source objective; low Z lowers phonon frequencies.
Binary compositions have few bonding modes, reducing peak intensity.
Halides lowered source objective; weak halogen bonds give low phonon energies.
Low mean Z covers light nonmetals and binaries.

skills.hypothesis: Reverses the low-confidence halogen and quinary-seinery source relations; fails if halides and binaries actually carry high-lying peaks.

lesson: The chalcogenide transfer failed: chalcogenide and post-transition candidates scored poorly, while the highest values came from lanthanide-free oxides. Development lifts and matched-rule evidence point to oxide polarizability and moderate concentration as the validated mechanisms.
revision_summary: Replaced the chalcogenide transfer with a polarizable oxide skill that keeps the moderate-concentration and mean-Z-mid rules but replaces chalcogenide with oxide and adds a no-lanthanide rule. Kept the light-element counter-hypothesis unchanged. Both skills use two-to-four mechanistically interpretable rules, and neither uses placeholder keys or target outcomes.
